deaths_dashboard.title: Climate-sensitive deaths dashboard
deaths_dashboard.lede: Demonstration dashboard built directly on the health_climate_daily dataset. It summarizes deaths in climate-sensitive groups, compares respiratory and circulatory subsets, and shows an exploratory monthly association with maximum temperature and precipitation.
deaths_dashboard.error: The dashboard could not be loaded.
deaths_dashboard.groups_note: Respiratory and circulatory subsets help open up the total climate-sensitive deaths. They are shown as monitored groups, not as mutually exclusive partitions of the total.
deaths_dashboard.groups_legend: Each bar sums the group's deaths over the whole period analyzed; groups may overlap and do not add up to the total.
deaths_dashboard.trend_note: The series aggregates climate-sensitive deaths by month to reveal seasonal variation and periods of higher concentration.
deaths_dashboard.trend_legend: Line and area show the total climate-sensitive deaths summed for each month; hover a point for the exact value.
deaths_dashboard.association_note: Each point represents one month. The chart compares the average monthly climate condition with the monthly total of climate-sensitive deaths; the line summarizes the linear trend.
deaths_dashboard.association_legend: Each point is one month; the dark line is the linear fit between the selected climate variable and the monthly death total.
deaths_dashboard.correlation_caveat: Simple correlation between monthly averages; it does not imply causation and does not control for other factors (e.g. infrastructure, age structure).

deaths_dashboard.table_note: Top 10 municipalities by total climate-sensitive deaths; Tmax and precipitation are period averages, not sums.

overview.title: climasusDB: an open integrated database for climate, environment and One Health in Brazil
overview.lede: climasusDB organizes public data on climate, environment and health in Brazil into an open, versioned database ready for reuse. It supports research, surveillance, visualization and digital products from a One Health perspective.
overview.institution_body: climasusDB is part of the Rondônia Climate and Health Center and the broader climaSUS ecosystem. Development is funded by INCT-CONEXAO (National Institute for Research and Center of Excellence in Knowledge of Western and Eastern Amazonia), with a focus on open infrastructure for analyzing climate risks and health outcomes in Brazil.

sections.title: What climasusDB is
body: It is the data component of climaSUS: an organized, versioned and documented layer that transforms public systems into analysis-ready datasets.

Health data currently comes from DATASUS; climate data includes observational sources such as INMET and gridded sources such as ERA5, CHIRPS, PRODES and CAMS. Methodological transformation is handled by the climasus4r package. The One Health framing guides integration across climate, environment and human health without implying that every domain, such as animal health, is already published.

sections.title: How it is structured
body: The architecture follows bronze, silver and gold layers. Bronze preserves raw or near-raw data; silver standardizes keys, dates and variables; gold publishes stable Parquet tables with provenance metadata embedded in the Arrow schema.

The data/public directory is exactly the layout intended for publication in a public bucket. The web app reads catalog.json and queries Parquet files through HTTP Range requests using DuckDB-WASM, without its own backend.

sections.title: Data formats
body: Parquet is the official canonical format for climasusDB. It preserves types, compresses well, works with DuckDB, R and Python, and supports efficient partial reads in the browser.
ZIP-compressed CSV is offered only for small or summarized datasets. XLSX is not published in the catalog because it is redundant, less suitable for versioning and fragile for large datasets.

sections.title: Publishing and citation
body: Operational data hosting should use a public bucket, such as Google Cloud Storage or Cloudflare R2. Zenodo should be used for archiving, DOI assignment and citation of closed releases.
This separation avoids using Zenodo as the atlas backend while preserving a citable, permanent and auditable copy of published data.

product_sections.title: Explore
body: The main interactive analysis area. It supports navigation by municipality, state, indicator group and time series. This version prioritizes a single simple, communicable indicator: deaths in climate-sensitive groups.

product_sections.title: Data Catalog
body: A navigable repository of the core datasets exposed to the public: INMET weather stations and the daily health-climate series. It shows version, schema, provenance, coverage and download links.

body: A curated showcase of uses and examples reusing datasets published by climasusDB in applications, dashboards, studies, training materials or prototypes.

data-model.title: Data model & provenance
body: Every Gold dataset published under data/public/gold/ is a Parquet file with provenance metadata embedded in the Arrow schema, under the "climasus_meta" key (written by climasus4r::write_parquet_climasus()). This metadata includes the source DATASUS system, pipeline stage, aggregation type, and a processing history.

Versioning follows vX.Y.Z per dataset (e.g. health_climate_daily/v1.0.0). The path is always gold/{dataset}/v{version}/uf={uf}/data.parquet — the schema is identical between synthetic and real versions, so nothing in the frontend needs to change when a dataset moves from prototype to real data.

The public catalog highlights two core datasets: health_climate_daily, the municipality-day table combining climate-sensitive deaths and daily climate, and dim_station, the INMET stations used in the integration. Other derived products may exist in the pipeline, but they stay out of the main navigation until they pass publication curation.
Each dataset has a sibling datapackage.json (Frictionless Data standard) with the full schema and the same provenance metadata.

querying.title: Querying with DuckDB-WASM
body: climasusDB has no backend: the browser runs a WebAssembly build of DuckDB and queries the published Parquet files directly via HTTP range requests — only the bytes needed for each query are downloaded.

The same Parquet files can be opened outside the platform, with no dependency on climasusDB at all: with the DuckDB CLI (SELECT * FROM read_parquet('URL')), with pandas/pyarrow in Python, or with arrow::read_parquet() in R.
Example query used by Explore: SELECT code_muni, avg(precip) FROM health_climate_daily GROUP BY code_muni.

catalog-contract.title: Catalog contract
body: catalog.json guarantees: dataset name, latest version, list of available versions, synthetic-data flag, relative Parquet path, and row count. The public interface filters this list to show only datasets curated for main navigation. datapackage.json guarantees the column schema and the full climasus_meta metadata.

Every dataset exposed in the Data Catalog follows this Frictionless Data contract. Technical or derived products may exist in the pipeline, but they enter public navigation only after schema, coverage, provenance and usage clarity are reviewed.

heat-cardio.title: Heat and mortality
body: This theme documents one methodological possibility in the climaSUS ecosystem: relating heat extremes to daily health and climate series by municipality.

In the current interface, public exploration focuses on health_climate_daily and the INMET station layer. Specialized models remain methodological pipeline documentation and are not shown as main Explore indicators.
Rondônia was the original case-study area for this approach; today the data structure supports national analyses as new products pass publication curation.
